source_metadata.title: Performance of Anti-Factor Xa Versus Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time for Heparin Monitoring Using Multiple Nomograms
source_metadata.design: Prospective nonrandomized anti-Xa cohort with historical aPTT control

atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to compare anti-factor Xa concentration versus aPTT monitoring across multiple indication-specific intravenous unfractionated heparin nomograms.
The study used a prospective nonrandomized anti-Xa cohort with an aPTT-based historical control at a single 757-bed academic tertiary care center.
The analysis included 201 patients receiving continuous intravenous UFH on cardiology units: 101 in the prospective anti-Xa cohort and 100 historical aPTT controls.

population.label: Patients receiving continuous IV UFH on cardiology units

atoms.canonical_statement: Prospective patients were a convenience sample of patients receiving continuous IV UFH on the cardiology units between March 30 and June 30, 2015; historical controls were treated on the same units immediately before anti-Xa implementation.

population.label: Study-eligible patients
inclusion_criteria: Continuous IV UFH on cardiology units
Prospective period March 30-June 30, 2015 or historical immediately preceding period

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients were excluded for IV UFH use under 24 hours, treatment interruption over 10 hours, or at least 25% deviation from documented nomogram dosing-adjustment or monitoring compliance.
In the prospective cohort, paired anti-Xa and aPTT samples were drawn, but UFH dose adjustment and monitoring decisions were based only on anti-Xa concentrations.

population.label: Patients treated under the corresponding indication-specific UFH nomogram

atoms.canonical_statement: DVT/PE adjustment rule: ≤48 seconds or anti-Xa ≤0.20 U/mL → 80 U/kg bolus and increase infusion 4 U/kg/h; 49-67 or 0.21-0.29 → 40 U/kg bolus and increase 2 U/kg/h; 68-106 or 0.3-0.7 → no change; 107-115 or 0.71-0.80 → decrease 2 U/kg/h; 116-125 or 0.81-0.99 → hold 1 hour then decrease 3 U/kg/h; >125 or ≥1.0 → hold 2 hours then decrease 4 U/kg/h.

population.label: Patients treated under the corresponding indication-specific UFH nomogram

atoms.canonical_statement: UA/NSTEMI adjustment rule: ≤48 seconds or anti-Xa ≤0.20 U/mL → 60 U/kg bolus and increase infusion 4 U/kg/h; 49-67 or 0.21-0.29 → 30 U/kg bolus (maximum 2,000 U) and increase 2 U/kg/h; 68-96 or 0.3-0.6 → no change; 97-115 or 0.61-0.80 → decrease 2 U/kg/h; 116-125 or 0.81-0.99 → hold 1 hour then decrease 3 U/kg/h; >125 or ≥1.0 → hold 2 hours then decrease 4 U/kg/h.

population.label: Patients treated under the corresponding indication-specific UFH nomogram

atoms.canonical_statement: Atrial fibrillation/postoperative adjustment rule: ≤48 seconds or anti-Xa ≤0.20 U/mL → 60 U/kg bolus and increase infusion 3 U/kg/h; 49-67 or 0.21-0.29 → 40 U/kg bolus and increase 2 U/kg/h; 68-82 or 0.3-0.45 → no change; 83-96 or 0.46-0.60 → hold 1 hour then decrease 1 U/kg/h; 97-106 or 0.61-0.70 → hold 1 hour then decrease 2 U/kg/h; 107-125 or 0.71-0.99 → hold 1 hour then decrease 4 U/kg/h; >125 or ≥1.0 → hold 2 hours then decrease 6 U/kg/h.

population.label: Patients treated under the corresponding indication-specific UFH nomogram

atoms.canonical_statement: Stroke/electrophysiology/VAD/high-risk-bleeding adjustment rule: ≤48 seconds or anti-Xa ≤0.20 U/mL → increase infusion 2 U/kg/h; 49-58 or 0.21-0.24 → increase 1 U/kg/h; 59-72 or 0.25-0.35 → no change; 73-82 or 0.36-0.45 → decrease 1 U/kg/h; 83-106 or 0.46-0.69 → hold 1 hour then decrease 2 U/kg/h; >106 or ≥0.70 → stop infusion and call the physician.

population.label: Patients treated under the corresponding indication-specific UFH nomogram

atoms.canonical_statement: DVT/PE, UA/NSTEMI, and atrial fibrillation/postoperative nomograms could be ordered with or without a bolus; no-bolus versions omitted initial and titration boluses, while the stroke/EP/VAD/high-risk-bleeding nomogram used no bolus.
For both monitoring strategies, laboratory testing occurred 6 hours after initiation and after rate changes until 2 consecutive therapeutic results were obtained; thereafter monitoring was daily.
The primary endpoint was time to therapeutic anticoagulation; therapeutic anticoagulation was defined as 2 consecutive laboratory values within the nomogram-specific therapeutic range.

outcome.definition: Time until 2 consecutive laboratory values were in therapeutic range

atoms.canonical_statement: Secondary endpoints included dose adjustments per 24 hours, aPTT/anti-Xa discordance, length of stay, and inpatient clinical outcomes while receiving UFH; VTE was the primary clinical outcome, with bleeding and mortality secondary clinical outcomes.

outcome.definition: Dose adjustments/24 h, discordance, length of stay, VTE, bleeding, mortality

atoms.canonical_statement: Discordance was defined as a therapeutic anti-Xa concentration paired with a subtherapeutic or supratherapeutic aPTT result.

Continuous variables were compared with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests as appropriate, categorical variables with Fisher exact tests, and subgroup analyses were performed by UFH nomogram and presence or absence of a starting bolus.

The anti-Xa and historical aPTT cohorts did not differ significantly in reported baseline age, race, body mass index, renal dysfunction, concurrent medications, heparin nomogram distribution, or use of a bolus.

atoms.canonical_statement: The single-center comparison used a retrospective historical aPTT arm, creating risk of missing or incomplete control data and temporal confounding.
Bleeding and thrombotic outcomes were captured at any time during UFH therapy, without evaluating whether events occurred during a therapeutic result or following a dose change.
Potential baseline nonpharmacologic confounders such as coagulation abnormalities, critical illness, and conditions associated with low antithrombin III activity were not collected.
No power calculation was performed to detect differences in clinical outcomes; the study was designed around feasibility of conversion and time to therapeutic anticoagulation.

The authors concluded that anti-Xa monitoring of IV UFH improved time to therapeutic anticoagulation and reduced dose adjustments across multiple indication-based nomograms, but larger controlled studies are needed to determine whether clinical outcomes improve.

extraction_limitations: The schema has no dedicated field for full heparin titration algorithms, so Table 2 rule families are represented as method atoms with table-row provenance.
No patient-level paired-sample denominator is reported for the 49% discordance and 35% therapeutic-agreement findings; the population is therefore labeled without an invented sample size.
Subgroup consistency by nomogram and bolus status is reported qualitatively in the article text without subgroup effect estimates in the main tables.
Atoms are language-model extracted and marked needs_review; no human verification status is asserted.
